clue.text: Reveal daughter is tight

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees
taken as written
close means tight, as in a close fit or close-knit

explanation.surface: A parent lets slip that their daughter is stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' suggests meanness in the surface, but here it means close-fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something known or expose it is to reveal it; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Dispose of in ditch

definitions.meaning: to get rid of something carelessly

explanation.surface: Throw something away into a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditch' looks like the noun, a trench, but it is the verb to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipping rubbish away or abandoning something unwanted are both senses of this one verb.

clue.text: A green cave in the east

parts.note: to sag is to sink or give way, to cave in
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A green-tinged cavern out in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cave' looks like a noun, a cavern; 'cave in' is the verb, to sink.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey-green colour named after the herb's leaves is one shade of green.

clue.text: Such pages have no security of tenure

definitions.text: Such pages have no security of tenure

parts.words: Such pages have no security of tenure
parts.note: pages in a ring binder can be taken out at any time, unlike bound ones, like tenants without fixed tenure

explanation.surface: Pages likened to tenants who can be evicted at will.
explanation.definitionFit: Binder sheets are not fixed in place, so they may be removed whenever wanted.

clue.text: Dress with bodice for a sister with right build

indicators.note: to build something is to put its parts together anew, so these letters are assembled in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A dress picked for a sister with the right figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'build' looks like a person's figure, but it is the anagram signal; 'for' only links the dress to its wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's dress with a top tailored like a shirt is a style of frock with a fitted bodice.

clue.text: Artist arrived first in judge's private room

indicators.note: the word first tells the solver that the piece for arrived comes ahead of the artist

parts.note: came means arrived
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist

explanation.surface: A painter turned up early at the judge's chambers.
explanation.walkthrough: A case heard 'in camera' is heard privately, originally in the judge's own chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Camera is Latin for chamber, and in law it names the room where a judge hears matters privately.

clue.text: A social event to embarrass

parts.note: a bash is an informal party

explanation.surface: A party designed to embarrass people.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone feel ashamed or awkward is to embarrass them.

clue.text: Performances where people lose their heads

definitions.meaning: carrying out or performing something, as in the playing of a piece

explanation.surface: Stage shows in which audiences go wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose their heads' reads as panic or excitement; it is literal beheading.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist's renderings and a headsman's killings share one word, from carrying something out.

clue.text: Has a dread of arrests

explanation.surface: Someone frightened of being taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both fearful anticipation and the police seizing a suspect.

clue.text: Pinkish white, like Miss Hawks in Show Boat

definitions.meaning: a creamy off-white paint colour named after a flowering tree
... Hawks is the heroine of the musical Show Boat

explanation.surface: A colour description compared to a heroine of a famous musical.
explanation.definitionFit: The paint shade takes its name from the tree's blossom, and the same flower name was given to the musical's heroine.

clue.text: Cosmetics brand increased in price

parts.note: a make is a brand of goods, as in a make of car
prices that have gone up have increased

explanation.surface: A beauty label has become more expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Face paint such as lipstick and powder is collectively the stuff people put on, the everyday name for cosmetics.

clue.text: Creating favourable impression in a satisfactory answer to clue

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
good means satisfactory
in crosswords a light is the answer entered in the grid

explanation.surface: A neat crossword answer makes a fine impression.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'light' is crossword jargon for an answer, the word written into the white squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Shown flatteringly, so that others think well of it, is an idiom for a favourable impression.

clue.text: Friendly Society's headquarters

parts.note: the Society of Friends is the Quakers, whose place of worship is the building where they gather

explanation.surface: The head office of a mutual insurance club.
explanation.walkthrough: A friendly society is a British mutual-aid insurance club; the clue really means the Religious Society of Friends, the Quakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Quakers call their place of worship by this name, so it is the base of the Society of Friends.

clue.text: Chased fame, perhaps, and became conscience-stricken

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words could be arranged otherwise, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A celebrity seeker feels guilty about pursuing renown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CHASED FAME. 'and became' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking embarrassed or guilty because of something done is to be conscience-stricken.

clue.text: Material directed to be soft-soaped

parts.note: flannel is a soft woollen material
led means directed or guided

explanation.surface: Fabric being sent off to be gently cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: To flannel, in British usage, is to flatter or talk evasively.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sweet-talked with flattery or evasive patter is being soft-soaped.

clue.text: Divide lire grabbed by swindle

indicators.note: something grabbed by another is held inside it, so the lire goes within the swindle

parts.note: to have someone is to cheat or swindle them, as in 'you've been had'
L is the abbreviation for lira, the old Italian currency

explanation.surface: Split the Italian money taken in a con.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut something into two equal parts is to divide it.

clue.text: Factor in the Orient that keeps a river looking silvery

indicators.note: something that keeps another holds it inside, so the river letter sits within the rest

parts.note: a factor is an agent who does business for another
taken as written
E stands for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: An eastern dealer guards a river that looks like silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that keeps' signals the container; the river letter lands after the opening A. 'Argentine' as silvery is an old poetic adjective, not only the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from Latin argentum, silver, so it describes something with a silvery look.

clue.text: Proposed name I don't alter

indicators.note: to alter something is to change it, so these letters are changed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A suggested name I won't change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alter' rearranges NAME I DONT; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Put forward as a candidate for a post is to be proposed.

clue.text: Statement of beliefs exploding Old Testament famines

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A creed blowing up the biblical famines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploding' scrambles OT plus FAMINES.
explanation.definitionFit: A published declaration of a party's or person's principles is a public statement of beliefs.

clue.text: Put back material dug out

indicators.note: something put back is turned around, so the fabric is read from its end

parts.note: denim is a hard-wearing cotton material

explanation.surface: Fabric that was excavated has been replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' turns DENIM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal or ore that is excavated from the ground has been extracted, or dug out.

clue.text: Carefree, though not in cycling gear

definitions.meaning: coasting on a bicycle without pedalling, with the drive disengaged

explanation.surface: Relaxed, though not dressed for a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling gear' looks like Lycra clothing; it is the bicycle's drive mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Coasting downhill without pedalling is the literal sense, and figuratively it means unconstrained and easygoing.

clue.text: She's disparaged as fussy when old

definitions.text: She's disparaged as fussy when old

parts.words: She's disparaged as fussy when old
parts.note: calling anyone an old something, meaning a fussy person, is a disparaging expression for an elderly female

explanation.surface: An elderly lady dismissed as fussy.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage an 'old woman' is a fussy, timid person of either sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A female adult is the person meant; the idiom 'old woman' disparages fussiness.

clue.text: Outrageous old emperor

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means outrageous

explanation.surface: A scandalous ancient ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Several Holy Roman Emperors bore this name, Otto the Great among them.

clue.text: One controlling pupil's reactions is 21, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the coloured ring in the eye that widens or narrows the pupil
a girl's name, an example of the answer to 21 down, a female person

explanation.surface: A teacher's control of a pupil's responses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' suggests a schoolchild; it is the eye's opening.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye's coloured ring adjusts the pupil, and the same word is a girl's name.

clue.text: Capital heading, perhaps on this regular feature

definitions.meaning: a pillar is topped by a capital, the decorated head of an architectural support
a newspaper slot written regularly by the same writer

explanation.surface: A capital-letter headline above a newspaper's weekly piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital heading' reads as a capital-letter headline; it is the architectural capital at the top of a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar wears a capital on top, and a regular newspaper article by a named writer goes by the same word.

clue.text: A good mixer, maybe, but a trouble-maker

definitions.meaning: a device that stirs or shakes liquids, as in a washing machine

explanation.surface: Someone sociable, maybe, but who stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good mixer' suggests a sociable person; it is a stirring machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The stirring paddle in a washing machine shares its name with a political rabble-rouser who stirs up unrest.

clue.text: Sanded slippery part of tennis court

indicators.note: slippery things slide about, so the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A sanded tennis court has become slippery in part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippery' rearranges SANDED. This is real tennis, the old indoor game, not lawn tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: In real tennis the gallery for spectators at the server's end of the court bears this name.

clue.text: Thoughtful boss taking notes of what is owed

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud, as on a shield
IOUs are written notes acknowledging a debt

explanation.surface: A careful employer collecting written debt acknowledgements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' suggests a manager; it is a raised ornamental knob. 'taking' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given to reading and reflection is bookish and thoughtful.
